claims.text: North Capitol Street Northwest & P Street Northwest had 43 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 7 pedestrians injured, 7 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.9 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got Leading Pedestrian Interval signals in 2019. Across the city: at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-19%, 95% interval -35% to +1%) could be zero. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence.
The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: not shown (at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-19%, 95% interval -35% to +1%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.3 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $442,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.7 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $230,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

The District Department of Transportation (DDOT) is responsible for North Capitol Street Northeast, North Capitol Street Northwest, P Street Northeast, P Street Northwest (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
